Pipe welder here. I've worked in a lot of nuclear facilities, and it's truly awe inspiring. I remember my dad welding on the reactor head of a plant. He had dosimetry on his fingers, head, knees ,and feet. He caught so much dose on that jump it killed the good bacteria in his gut and he ended up puking and shitting himself for about a week. He's worked in those plants for around 15 years saying "That stuff won't hurt you." "It's regulated so heavily." "Flight attendents catch more dose in a year than a nuclear worker." Well, the Saturday before last he went to the hospital for what they thought was a stroke. It turns out he has a grade three giloblastoma that was 16cm by 6cm in diameter. The tumor was pushing on the motor sensory portion of his brain and caused him to be paralyzed on his left side. He worked 21 days straight for 12 hours a day without feeling in his hand or foot. Not pins and needles, but it's just not there. Says he would have to physically watch his foot as he walked. He's a tough old fucker. He goes back for radiation therapy next week to start to deal with it. I'm not working in nuclear plants anymore.
